report.title: Checkout: applying SAVE10 coupon renders Discount -$NaN and Total $NaN
report.summary: On http://localhost:4401/checkout, applying the valid coupon code SAVE10 to the checkout causes the Discount and Total rows to display NaN instead of the calculated amounts.

steps.action: Click the Coupon input (placeholder "Enter code").
Type the coupon code SAVE10 into the Coupon input.
Click the Apply coupon button.
Observe the Discount and Total rows: Discount shows -$NaN and Total shows $NaN (bug reproduced).

report.expected: With cart subtotal $144.00 and a valid 10% SAVE10 coupon, Discount should show -$14.40 and Total should show $129.60.
report.actual: Discount shows -$NaN and Total shows $NaN; the line-item prices remain $120.00 and $24.00.
report.suspectedCause: The coupon API returns a successful response {"code":"SAVE10","valid":true,"percent_off":10}, but checkout.js:12 reads `.rate` from an undefined object (TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'rate') at HTMLButtonElement.<anonymous> (http://localhost:4401/static/js/checkout.js:12:39)). The apply-coupon handler likely expects a coupon object with a `rate` property, while the API field is `percent_off` (and possibly returns the coupon payload nested or under a different key), so the discount rate is undefined and propagates into the formatted Discount and Total as NaN. Check the response parsing and the property used for the discount rate in checkout.js around line 12, and guard against a missing/non-numeric rate before computing the total.
evidence: Console error at 1.6s: "TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'rate')" at http://localhost:4401/static/js/checkout.js:12:39
Console log at 1.6s: "coupon response {\"code\":\"SAVE10\",\"valid\":true,\"percent_off\":10}"
Network at 1.6s: GET http://localhost:4401/api/coupons/SAVE10 -> 200, response {\"code\":\"SAVE10\",\"valid\":true,\"percent_off\":10}

security.issue: A Stripe live secret key was exposed in a GET request URL
security.evidence: GET http://localhost:4401/api/coupons/SAVE10?token=[redacted stripe-live-key] (1.6s) — the value was actually sent by the page and appears in URL query string, where it is retained in browser history, server/proxy access logs, and Referer headers.

agent.evidence: After typing SAVE10 and clicking Apply coupon, the Discount row rendered "-$NaN" and Total rendered "$NaN" (instead of -$14.40 and $129.60). Line items remained $120.00 and $24.00. Console also logged: TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'rate').
trace: {"type":"done","reproduced":true,"evidence":"After typing SAVE10 and clicking Apply coupon, the Discount row rendered \"-$NaN\" and Total rendered \"$NaN\" (instead of -$14.40 and $129.60). Line items remained $120.00 and $24.00. Console also logged: TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'rate')."}

fix.explanation: The coupon API returns the percentage in `percent_off`, but `applyCoupon` read `coupon.discount.rate`, which is undefined, so the multiplication produced NaN. The pricing helper now reads/validates `percent_off`, and the checkout handler rejects invalid responses instead of logging a synthetic TypeError, so the discount and total are computed from the real API field.

report.title: Profile display name fails to save on /profile (POST /api/profile returns 500: missing profiles.display_name column)
report.summary: On http://localhost:4401/profile, editing the Display name field to "Priya S." and clicking "Save changes" returns a server error and the change is not persisted. The API response indicates the profiles table is missing the display_name column.

steps.action: The /profile page loads with the Display name field containing "Priya Sharma".
Replace the Display name value with "Priya S." (input[text]#name).
Click "Save changes" (button#save).
Network: POST http://localhost:4401/api/profile → 500, request body {"displayName":"Priya S."}; response: {"error":"column \"display_name\" of relation \"profiles\" does not exist"}.
A toast appears reading "Profile saved ✓" even though the request failed with HTTP 500.
The page is reloaded/navigated to http://localhost:4401/profile.
The Display name field shows "Priya Sharma" again; the edited value "Priya S." was not saved.

report.expected: Saving the edited display name "Priya S." succeeds (2xx), the name persists across reload as "Priya S.", and a success toast is only shown when the request actually succeeds.
report.actual: The save request fails with HTTP 500: {"error":"column \"display_name\" of relation \"profiles\" does not exist"}. The UI nevertheless displays a "Profile saved ✓" toast, and after reloading /profile the Display name field shows the original "Priya Sharma" instead of "Priya S.".
report.suspectedCause: The profiles table (or the migration/schema applied to it) has no display_name column, so the UPDATE/INSERT in the POST /api/profile handler fails at the database layer. Check the profiles table definition/migrations for a display_name column (and ensure the migration is applied to the database being used by the API), plus the field/column mapping in the /api/profile route. Secondary issue: the client shows the success toast without checking the response status, so a 500 is reported as "Profile saved ✓".
evidence: [0.8s] POST http://localhost:4401/api/profile → 500 11ms
request body: {"displayName":"Priya S."}
response: {"error":"column \"display_name\" of relation \"profiles\" does not exist"}
Frame at 1.5s shows toast: "Profile saved ✓"
Frame at 2.3s shows Display name reverted to "Priya Sharma"

agent.evidence: Set Display name to "Priya S." and clicked "Save changes". The UI immediately displayed a "Profile saved ✓" toast. After navigating back to /profile, the Display name field again showed "Priya Sharma", so the edited value was not persisted while a success toast was shown (matching the reported failed-save / false-success symptom).
trace: {"type":"done","reproduced":true,"evidence":"Set Display name to \"Priya S.\" and clicked \"Save changes\". The UI immediately displayed a \"Profile saved ✓\" toast. After navigating back to /profile, the Display name field again showed \"Priya Sharma\", so the edited value was not persisted while a success toast was shown (matching the reported failed-save / false-success symptom)."}

fix.explanation: The profile row exposes its display name as the `name` column, but the API updated a nonexistent `display_name` column, causing every save to fail. The route now updates `name`; the client also checks `res.ok` so the success toast is only shown for a successful response, while failures produce an error toast.

Check the Orders nav link definition in the header component and the client-side router route table for the account orders page. Since there are no console or network entries, the failure is handled locally by the app's not-found route.

report.title: Valid alert email rejected on Settings page — "priya+alerts@example.com" fails email validation
report.summary: On the Settings page (http://localhost:4401/settings), entering the valid alert address `priya+alerts@example.com` and clicking **Save settings** does not save. The form shows the inline error "Please enter a valid email address." and the browser console logs `email validation failed priya+alerts@example.com`. No network request is issued, so the failure occurs entirely in client-side validation before the save request is sent.

steps.action: On the Settings page, the **Notification settings** card shows the **Alert email** field pre-filled with `priya@example.com`.
In the **Alert email** field, replaced the value with `priya+alerts@example.com`.
Clicked the **Save settings** button.
The form did not save: the field still shows `priya+alerts@example.com` and a red inline error appeared below it reading "Please enter a valid email address." No success confirmation is shown.

report.expected: Saving the valid email address `priya+alerts@example.com` succeeds — no validation error is displayed and the setting is persisted (a save request is sent).
report.actual: Saving shows the red validation message "Please enter a valid email address." for `priya+alerts@example.com`. The value is not saved and no network request is made.
report.suspectedCause: Client-side email validation rejects the `+` sub-address tag (RFC 5322 allows `+` in the local part). The console warning `email validation failed priya+alerts@example.com` confirms the value is rejected by the client-side validator before any request is made (NETWORK: none). Check the email regex/validator used by the `Alert email` input on the Settings form — it likely lacks support for `+` (and possibly other valid local-part characters) in the local-part of the address, e.g. a pattern that only permits `[A-Za-z0-9._-]` before the `@`. Prefer browser-native constraint validation (`type="email"` / `input.validity`) or a standards-compliant check rather than a custom regex. Also verify that the form's submit handler is not independently re-running the same faulty check.
evidence: CONSOLE [0.8s] warn: email validation failed priya+alerts@example.com
NETWORK (0) — no requests were issued after clicking Save settings
Frame at t=1.5s: inline red error "Please enter a valid email address." beneath the field containing `priya+alerts@example.com`

agent.evidence: Replaced Alert email with priya+alerts@example.com and clicked Save settings. The page displayed the red inline error "Please enter a valid email address.", the field retained the value, no success confirmation appeared, and the console logged "email validation failed priya+alerts@example.com".
trace: {"type":"done","reproduced":true,"evidence":"Replaced Alert email with priya+alerts@example.com and clicked Save settings. The page displayed the red inline error \"Please enter a valid email address.\", the field retained the value, no success confirmation appeared, and the console logged \"email validation failed priya+alerts@example.com\"."}

fix.explanation: The custom `isValidEmail` regex allowed only `[A-Za-z0-9._-]` in the local part and a single-label domain, so `+` sub-addresses and multi-level domains were rejected client-side before any request was made. I replaced it with a standards-oriented pattern that supports RFC-style local-part characters (including `+`) and multi-label domains, and made the Settings save actually POST and persist the value through a new `/api/settings` endpoint that revalidates server-side, with the client showing an error if the server rejects the save.

report.title: Cart quantity increments by 2 on a single click of "Increase quantity" (Trail runners goes 1 → 3, subtotal $120.00 → $360.00)
report.summary: On http://localhost:4401/cart, clicking the "Increase quantity" (+) button once for the Trail runners row increases the displayed quantity from 1 to 3 instead of to 2. The subtotal correspondingly changes from $120.00 to $360.00 (3 × $120.00).

steps.action: Initial state of the cart page shows the "Trail runners" line item with quantity 1 and a Subtotal of $120.00.
Click the blue "+" button labeled "Increase quantity" for the Trail runners item.
After the single click, the quantity for Trail runners is shown as 3 and the Subtotal as $360.00. Bug reproduced.

report.expected: One click of "Increase quantity" should change the Trail runners quantity from 1 to 2, with the subtotal updating to $240.00 (2 × $120.00).
report.actual: One click of "Increase quantity" changes the quantity from 1 to 3, and the subtotal becomes $360.00 (3 × $120.00).
report.suspectedCause: The quantity increment handler in the cart page likely applies the increment twice — e.g. an updateQuantity(+1) call executed both in the button's onClick handler and again in a parent/listener or via double event binding (double-registered handler, duplicated effect, or a loop that adds the step twice). No console errors or network requests were captured, so the doubling appears to be entirely client-side in the click handler. Check the "Increase quantity" button's click handler and any shared cart-line update callback for duplicate invocation, and confirm the state update uses a single +1 per event.
evidence: Frame t=0.0s: quantity "1", Subtotal "$120.00"
Frame t=0.8s: quantity "3", Subtotal "$360.00"
ACTIONS: [0.1s] click button#plus "Increase quantity" — only one click recorded
CONSOLE: (none)
NETWORK: (none)

agent.evidence: Initial cart showed Trail runners quantity 1 with Subtotal $120.00. After a single click on the blue "+" (Increase quantity, #plus) button, the quantity displayed 3 and the Subtotal became $360.00 — matching the reported bug instead of the expected quantity 2 / $240.00.
trace: {"type":"done","reproduced":true,"evidence":"Initial cart showed Trail runners quantity 1 with Subtotal $120.00. After a single click on the blue \"+\" (Increase quantity, #plus) button, the quantity displayed 3 and the Subtotal became $360.00 — matching the reported bug instead of the expected quantity 2 / $240.00."}

fix.explanation: The cart's "+" listener calls `nextQuantity` exactly once per click, but `nextQuantity` in `public/js/lib/cart.js` increments by 2 (`q + 2`), so a quantity of 1 becomes 3 and the subtotal becomes 3 × price. Changing the step to 1 makes one click yield 2 while preserving the max-quantity clamp.

results.title: Checkout scrolls sideways on my phone

report.title: Checkout page scrolls horizontally on mobile; coupon row (476px) overflows 360px/390px viewports
report.summary: At 360px and 390px widths, the checkout document is 476px wide, causing 116px and 86px of horizontal overflow respectively. The culprit is the coupon row (div.row.coupon-row), whose right edge extends to 476px and is clipped off-screen; the blue "Apply coupon" button is only partially visible (at 360px only its left edge is shown, at 390px only "App" is shown). The layout is correct from 768px upward, so this is a mobile-only CSS/responsive bug.

steps.action: Open /checkout at a 360px-wide viewport. The page renders with the header wrapped onto two lines ("Acme Outfitters | Cart | Checkout | Profile" / "Settings | Orders | Sign out"), but the coupon row is pushed beyond the right edge. The "Apply coupon" button is clipped, showing only its left rounded edge.
Scroll the page horizontally: the content can be dragged 116px to the right, revealing the off-screen "Apply coupon" button while leaving a blank/empty band on the left of the page.
Repeat at a 390px-wide viewport: the page is still 476px wide (86px overflow) and the "Apply coupon" button is still clipped (label shows "App" before being cut off). Same coupon-row overflow.
Check wider viewports for comparison: at 768px, 1024px and 1440px the page width matches the viewport (no horizontal overflow) and the coupon row, input and button all fit inside the card.

report.expected: At 360px and 390px the checkout content fits the viewport width with no horizontal scrolling; the full "Apply coupon" button is visible next to the Coupon / "Enter code" input.
report.actual: Document width is 476px at both 360px and 390px viewports, producing 116px and 86px of horizontal scroll. The coupon row's right edge is at 476px, so the "Apply coupon" button is cut off by the viewport edge. The header nav also wraps to two lines on mobile.
report.suspectedCause: The checkout card / .coupon-row has a fixed minimum width (or fixed-width flex children and/or a fixed padding) of ~476px, so it cannot shrink below that on narrow screens. Likely the row is a flex container without `min-width: 0` / `flex-wrap`, and the card container lacks `max-width: 100%` / `box-sizing: border-box`; alternatively the card has a hard-coded width (e.g. 420px + padding). Check the checkout CSS for the card container and `.row.coupon-row` rules and add a mobile breakpoint so the row stacks (label + input, then full-width button) and the card is capped at 100% width.
evidence: 360px viewport: page width 476px, horizontal overflow 116px; div.row.coupon-row right edge at 476px (viewport 360px)
390px viewport: page width 476px, horizontal overflow 86px; div.row.coupon-row right edge at 476px (viewport 390px)
768px / 1024px / 1440px viewports: page width equals viewport width, no overflow recorded
Screenshots at 360px and 390px show the blue "Apply coupon" button clipped by the right viewport edge (only its left edge / "App" visible)

layout.issue: Row is wider than the viewport (page 476px vs viewport 360px, 116px overflow); the Apply coupon button is clipped off-screen.
layout.suggestion: Cap the checkout card at `max-width: 100%; box-sizing: border-box;` and let the coupon row shrink/wrap: `.coupon-row { display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:8px; }` with `.coupon-row > * { min-width:0; }` and a mobile rule making the Apply button `flex: 1 1 100%;`

layout.issue: Row is wider than the viewport (page 476px vs viewport 390px, 86px overflow); the Apply coupon button label is cut off.
layout.suggestion: Same as 360px: allow the coupon row to wrap and the button to take a full-width line under the input on narrow screens.

layout.element: header nav links (Cart, Checkout, Profile, Settings, Orders, Sign out)
layout.issue: Tap targets are only 21px tall (e.g. Cart 28x21, Checkout 62x21, Profile 41x21, Settings 53x21, Orders 44x21, Sign out 53x21), below the 44px minimum; nav wraps onto two lines on mobile.
layout.suggestion: Give nav links `display:inline-block; padding:10px 8px;` (or `min-height:44px`) so they meet the recommended touch target size.

layout.element: header nav links (Cart, Checkout, Profile, Settings, Orders, Sign out)
layout.issue: Tap targets are only 21px tall, below the 44px minimum.
layout.suggestion: Same as 360px: add vertical padding / min-height to nav links.

layout.issue: Tap targets are only 21px tall at 768px as well.
layout.suggestion: Increase link tap area (padding or min-height 44px) for touch devices.

layout.issue: Tap targets are only 21px tall at 1024px as well.
layout.suggestion: Increase link tap area (padding or min-height 44px) for touch devices.

layout.issue: Tap targets are only 21px tall at 1440px as well.
layout.suggestion: Increase link tap area (padding or min-height 44px) for touch devices.

fix.explanation: The horizontal overflow came from the coupon row's hard-coded `min-width: 460px`, which forced its children beyond the card at mobile widths. Removing that floor and allowing the label and button to occupy full-width lines on small screens keeps the row within the card, while increasing the header links' height and padding fixes their undersized tap targets.
